clinician.trajectory_summary: A 46-year-old Ghanaian male presented to the outpatient department with painless total hematuria and left flank pain (dull, constant, non-radiating). Physical examination revealed elevated blood pressure (154/112 mmHg) with no abdominal mass or tenderness. CT imaging of the abdomen and pelvis on admission demonstrated bilateral enlarged kidneys (right 18.8 × 8.0 cm, left 21 × 9.8 cm) with innumerable cysts of varying sizes replacing the renal parenchyma, and the right kidney was ectopically located in the right aspect of the pelvis. Laboratory evaluation revealed hemoglobin 13.2 g/dl and significantly deranged renal function with creatinine 518 μmol/l and eGFR 13 ml/min, indicating advanced chronic kidney disease (Stage 5). The patient was initiated on antihypertensive therapy and analgesia for flank pain, with referral to urology and nephrology departments for ongoing management.
